title: TEAD4 Regulates apical domain homeostasis and cell-positioning to maintain the trophectoderm lineage during mouse blastocyst development
abstractText: Abstract In mammalian preimplantation embryos, distinct cell lineages occupy defined spatial niches. The outer trophectoderm (TE) forms an epithelial monolayer surrounding the inner cell mass (ICM) and blastocyst cavity. In mice, the Tead4 gene encodes a polarity-dependent transcription factor required for TE specification. Here, we demonstrate that Tead4 also preserves TE integrity during blastocyst maturation. Clonal siRNA-mediated Tead4 knockdown (KD) disrupts outer cell apical domain morphology, causing abnormal allocation of these clones to an enlarged ICM, despite minimal impact on established polarity. Fixed sample and live embryo light-sheet microscopy imaging reveal that TEAD4-deficient outer cells atypically migrate into the blastocyst ICM, sometimes via apical domain abscission, or are repositioned post-division, linking disrupted apical domain morphology to altered spatial positioning and fate. Transcriptomic analysis indicates that TEAD4 regulates genes involved in cytoskeletal organization, particularly those related to actin and cell adhesion, which we propose are critical for maintaining outer cell TE positioning. Combined KD of Tead4 and two of its targets, the atypical GTPases Rnd1 and Rnd3, partially rescues misallocation but does not prevent apical morphological abnormalities. These findings indicate TEAD4 and its downstream regulatory network actively contribute to blastocyst TE maintenance, beyond initial specification, up until the peri-implantation stage, ensuring proper lineage segregation.

abstractText: This study was motivated by the low mathematical problem-solving abilities of elementary school students, particularly regarding probability concepts encompassing understanding problems, devising plans, carrying out procedures, and looking back at solutions. This condition was exacerbated by conventional teaching practices that lacked interactive digital media integration. This study aimed to examine differences in sixth-grade students' problem-solving abilities in probability following the implementation of the Problem-Based Learning (PBL) model assisted by the Quizizz application. A quantitative quasi-experimental approach employing a pretest-posttest control group design was applied, involving 38 sixth-grade students divided into 23 students from SDN 1 Bakalan (experimental group) and 15 students from SDN 3 Bakalan (control group). Data were gathered through validated subjective essay tests and analyzed using the Wilcoxon Signed Rank Test. The results demonstrated that the control class average increased from 21.33 to 37.00, whereas the experimental class increased substantially from 31.09 to 78.69. The non-parametric hypothesis test yielded an Asymp. Sig. (2-tailed) value of 0.001 (p<0.05). Consequently, there is a statistically significant difference in sixth-grade students' mathematical problem-solving abilities after experiencing the Quizizz-assisted Problem-Based Learning model. ABSTRAK Penelitian ini dilatarbelakangi oleh rendahnya kemampuan pemecahan masalah matematis siswa sekolah dasar, khususnya pada materi peluang yang mencakup tahapan memahami masalah, menyusun rencana, melaksanakan penyelesaian, dan memeriksa kembali hasil pekerjaan. Kondisi tersebut diperparah oleh proses pembelajaran konvensional yang belum mengintegrasikan media digital interaktif. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menguji perbedaan kemampuan pemecahan masalah matematika siswa kelas VI pada materi peluang setelah diterapkannya model Problem-Based Learning (PBL) berbantuan aplikasi Quizizz. Metode penelitian yang digunakan adalah kuantitatif melalui eksperimen semu (quasi-experiment) dengan desain pretest-posttest control group design. Subjek penelitian melibatkan 38 siswa kelas VI yang terbagi atas 23 siswa SDN 1 Bakalan sebagai kelas eksperimen dan 15 siswa SDN 3 Bakalan sebagai kelas kontrol. Data dikumpulkan menggunakan instrumen tes uraian yang telah teruji validitas dan reliabilitasnya, kemudian dianalisis menggunakan uji statistik nonparametrik Wilcoxon Signed Rank Test. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan peningkatan nilai rata-rata kelas kontrol dari 21,33 menjadi 37,00, sedangkan kelas eksperimen mengalami lonjakan dari 31,09 menjadi 78,69. Uji hipotesis menghasilkan nilai Asymp. Sig. (2-tailed) sebesar 0,001 (p<0,05). title: Computer-Aided Process Planning and its Integration with ERP and MRP Systems: A Systematic Review
abstractText: In today's manufacturing industry, Computer-Aided Process Planning (CAPP) is an important tool that helps to convert design information into manufacturing plans efficiently. With the changing dynamics of manufacturing environments with a greater focus on digital integration, integration of CAPP with Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) and Material Requirements Planning (MRP) systems becomes significant to achieve operational efficiency. This systematic review is a review of current status and the challenges of digital integration of the CAPP and ERP/MRP systems in the context of Computer Integrated Manufacturing (CIM). The purpose of this paper is to shed light on the dominant approaches, challenges of integration, benefits, and technology trends that emerged from various studies. The aim of the review is to create an organised knowledge base for researchers and practitioners that will help them to make the process planning workflow more optimised, by using better ERP and MRP integration, to set in motion improved resource utilization, production scheduling and decision making. The review is conducted following a documented protocol, according to PRISMA. The CAPP terms were searched in Scopus, Web of Science, IEEE Xplore, ScienceDirect and Google Scholar along with ERP, MRP, integration and interoperability terms and only the peer-reviewed English literature published from 2016 to 2025 were included. Titles, abstracts and full texts were screened by two reviewers against pre-stated eligibility criteria, data was extracted on a standard form, the quality of the studies was appraised with a checklist and the 22 included studies were organised on a taxonomy of integration level, CAPP approach (variant, generative, hybrid), enterprise-system scope, enabling technology, and application domain. The synthesis reveals a transition towards STEP-based data exchange, service-oriented architectures, ontology-based and digital-twin architectures, but little evidence of end-to-end integration, especially for SMEs and manufacturers in developing countries. The review is offered as a guide for researchers and practitioners interested in making a step towards closing the gap between design and process planning and enterprise planning.

title: Freeze–thaw cycles alter soil pore-size distribution and enhance soil water accumulation under no–tillage on the Loess Plateau
Topology Optimization and Generative Design in Additive Manufacturing: A Systematic Review of Algorithms, Tools and Industrial Applications
abstractText: Additive manufacturing (AM) has increased the design space of engineering components, allowing the creation of geometries which are hard or even impossible to realise through conventional machining, casting and forming. The capacity has added to the curiosity surrounding generative design (GD) and topology optimisation (TO), which aim to enhance structural performance, minimise material consumption and investigate other design options. This review combines the technical compilation provided with the relevant scholarly literature on the relationship between TO, GD and AM. The review is organised around the reporting principles of PRISMA 2020 and focuses specifically on the review question, eligibility logic, organisation of the evidence, methodological limitations and research gaps. Literature suggests that density-based approaches like Solid Isotropic Material with Penalisation (SIMP), level-set methods and evolutionary techniques continue to be important TO approaches, and GD is a broader requirements-driven approach which can involve optimisation, simulation, materials selection, and manufacturing constraints. The key result here is that having the best solution in the world of computation does not guarantee the best solution in the world of manufacturing, economy and reliability. All of these, such as overhangs, support structure, build orientation, enclosed voids, minimum feature size, anisotropy, residual stress, thermal distortion, surface finish, post-processing and cost, need to be taken into consideration in the design process. Applications in the aerospace, automotive and lightweight cellular structures sectors show promising potential, but benefits have only been reported in the context of specific applications. The next step in research should focus on coupled design–process optimisation, multi-physics modelling, uncertainty quantification, explainable artificial intelligence, experimental validation and closed-loop digital manufacturing. The synthesis is also embedded in the setting of an industrial economy, where knowledge and skills about the processes, their parameters and constraints determine what can be practically achieved, and in which limited use of AM and simulation tools is prevalent. The review finds that the maturity of TO and GD should be assessed based on the quality of validated engineering outcomes and not just on the geometric complexity or weight reduction alone.

title: Ex situ thermal acclimation alters temperature selection with limited post-release effects in an endangered frog ( Rana muscosa )
abstractText: Abstract Amphibian declines driven by the fungal pathogen Batrachochytrium dendrobatidis (Bd) pose major challenges for conservation, particularly for cold-adapted species occupying habitats where temperatures may be less limiting to Bd growth. Host thermal behaviour can influence infection dynamics, and thermal environments during developmental stages may shape disease susceptibility and performance. We tested whether exposing endangered mountain yellow-legged frogs (Rana muscosa) to different developmental ex situ thermal treatments prior to a reintroduction event altered selected temperature and post-release habitat use, Bd outcomes and apparent survival. Temperature-selection trials revealed that selected temperature was moderately repeatable among individuals. Contrary to predictions, frogs reared in a high temperature treatment subsequently selected cooler temperatures than frogs reared under standard conditions. After release at a Bd-positive site, high temperature treatment frogs exhibited marginally higher short-term apparent survival. However, survival declined rapidly regardless of treatment and we found no treatment-based differences in microhabitat use or Bd patterns, possibly due to low detection rates in the field. These results demonstrate that R. muscosa shifts selected temperature in response to thermal acclimation during rearing, but that such shifts may not translate to improved establishment in Bd-positive environments. Optimizing reintroduction outcomes for Bd-susceptible amphibians will likely require combining husbandry-based thermal conditioning with complementary Bd mitigation strategies.

Bony labyrinth taxonomic identification and long-term evolution of livestock in the Southwest and Central Asia
abstractText: Abstract Southwest and Central Asia were pivotal regions for the domestication and dispersal of domestic herbivores. Here we investigate long-term variation in bony labyrinth morphology of domestic bovids (sheep, goats and cattle) across the last 10 000 years. We focused on the osseous cavity of the inner ear, located within the petrous bone. We analysed semicircular canal (SC) size and shape using micro-computed tomography and geometric morphometrics (GMM) on 78 modern reference specimens and 234 archaeological petrous bones from 51 sites spanning the Iranian Plateau, Central Asia, the Caucasus and the Indus Valley. Bony labyrinth morphometrics yielded a strong taxonomic signal, enabling species-level identification of 228 out of 234 specimens and revealing greater diversity than anticipated. Comparative analyses further documented contrasting, nonlinear diachronic trajectories in SC size and shape among sheep, goats and cattle, reflecting species-specific responses to domestication and long-term herd management. Together, these results demonstrate that bony labyrinth GMM provides a robust, non-destructive framework for taxonomic identification and evolutionary inference and underscore how long-term, interdisciplinary approaches can capture the complex, nonlinear dynamics of animal domestication across the longue durée.
